promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

learningObjectives.title: The nuclear model of the atom
Detection and types of nuclear emission

questions.q: Which two types of particle are found in the nucleus of an atom?
questions.explain: The nucleus contains positively charged protons and uncharged neutrons, with electrons orbiting outside it.

questions.q: In the alpha-particle scattering experiment, most alpha particles passed straight through the thin gold foil. What does this indicate about the atom?
options: Most of the atom is empty space
Electrons are packed in the nucleus
questions.explain: Undeflected particles show that atoms are mostly empty space with a very small nucleus.

questions.q: A very small fraction of alpha particles were deflected back through large angles. What does this suggest about the nucleus?
options: It is small, dense and positively charged
It is large and negatively charged
questions.explain: Back-scattering shows the positive charge and most of the mass are concentrated in a tiny dense nucleus.

questions.q: The proton number (atomic number) of a nucleus is the number of...
questions.explain: The proton number Z counts the protons; the nucleon number A counts protons plus neutrons.

questions.q: A nucleus has a nucleon number of 23 and a proton number of 11. How many neutrons does it contain?
questions.explain: Number of neutrons = nucleon number - proton number = 23 - 11 = 12.

questions.q: Isotopes of the same element have...
options: the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons
the same number of neutrons but different numbers of protons
different numbers of both protons and neutrons
questions.explain: Isotopes share proton number (same element) but differ in neutron number, giving different nucleon numbers.

questions.q: Radioactive decay is best described as a process that is...
questions.explain: Decay of any individual nucleus is random and spontaneous, unaffected by temperature or chemical state.

questions.q: Which instrument is commonly used to detect and measure radioactivity?
questions.explain: A Geiger-Müller tube connected to a counter registers ionising radiation as counts.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a source of background radiation?
questions.explain: Sound is not ionising radiation; radon, cosmic rays and rocks are genuine background sources.

questions.q: An alpha particle is best described as...
options: a helium nucleus (2 protons and 2 neutrons)
questions.explain: An alpha particle consists of two protons and two neutrons, identical to a helium nucleus, with charge +2.

questions.q: Which type of nuclear radiation is stopped by a single sheet of paper?
questions.explain: Alpha radiation has low penetration and is stopped by paper or a few centimetres of air.

questions.q: Which list orders the three radiations from most ionising to least ionising?
questions.explain: Alpha is the most strongly ionising and gamma the least, in reverse order to their penetrating power.

questions.q: Beta radiation is best stopped by...
questions.explain: Beta particles pass through paper but are absorbed by a few millimetres of aluminium.

questions.q: When passed through an electric or magnetic field, which radiation is NOT deflected?
questions.explain: Gamma rays carry no charge, so a field cannot deflect them, unlike charged alpha and beta particles.

questions.q: When a nucleus emits an alpha particle, how do its numbers change?
options: Nucleon number decreases by 4 and proton number decreases by 2
Nucleon number decreases by 2 and proton number decreases by 4
Nucleon number is unchanged and proton number increases by 1
questions.explain: Losing an alpha particle (2 protons, 2 neutrons) reduces the nucleon number by 4 and the proton number by 2.

questions.q: When a nucleus emits a beta particle, the...
options: proton number increases by 1 while the nucleon number stays the same
proton number decreases by 1 while the nucleon number stays the same
questions.explain: A neutron changes into a proton and an emitted electron, so proton number rises by 1 and nucleon number is unchanged.

questions.q: A nucleus with nucleon number 214 and proton number 82 emits a beta particle. What are its new numbers?
questions.explain: Beta emission raises the proton number by 1 to 83 and leaves the nucleon number at 214.

questions.q: The half-life of a radioactive isotope is the time taken for...
options: half of the undecayed nuclei to decay
all of the nuclei to decay
the mass of the sample to double
questions.explain: Half-life is the time for half the remaining undecayed nuclei (or the activity) to fall to half its value.

questions.q: A source has an activity of 800 Bq and a half-life of 5 minutes. What is its activity after 15 minutes?
questions.explain: 15 minutes is three half-lives, so activity halves three times: 800 → 400 → 200 → 100 Bq.

questions.q: The count rate from a source falls from 240 counts/s to 30 counts/s in 9 hours. What is the half-life?
questions.explain: 240 → 120 → 60 → 30 is three halvings over 9 hours, so each half-life is 3 hours.
